title: Few-Shot Examples and Structured Outputs
summary: Examples in the prompt teach a model a task without changing its weights, and schemas plus constrained decoding make its output machine-readable every time. This lesson puts numbers on both: what an example is worth, and what a format error costs at scale.
objectives: Explain in-context learning as conditioning, and compute how examples shift a model's belief about which task it is doing
Decide how many few-shot examples to include by weighing their token cost against the errors they prevent
Choose examples by similarity, diversity and label balance, and avoid ordering and majority-label biases
Compute the probability of at least one malformed output over N calls and the effect of validate-and-retry
Apply constrained decoding by masking logits and renormalising the softmax, and explain what it does not guarantee
prerequisites: You should be comfortable with softmax over logits and sampling from [Next-token prediction and sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling), cosine similarity from [Embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings), and token costs from [Anatomy of a Prompt](/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-anatomy).
